# Central-bank playbooks (G10)

Dated snapshots from the cited sources. Levels go stale. Re-read the current state from the canonical tables
(`cb_meetings`, `rate_fixings`, `stir_quotes`, `macro_series`) before using any level here. Rows marked "thin" have
little source coverage; do not fill the gaps from memory.

Forecast-meeting months are a 2018 empirical count (swapsball, Central bank decisions and inflation forecasts,
8 Mar 2018): Fed and ECB Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec; BoE and RBA Feb/May/Aug/Nov; BoC Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct. Re-test them on the
current `cb_meetings` table, since the Fed and ECB calendars and BoC rules have changed since.

| CB | Mandate and framework | Operating system (dated) | Reaction-function features | Key gauges and dated readings |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fed (USD) | Dual mandate. Flexible inflation targeting since the 2025 framework review (no make-up, no ELB, balanced approach when goals conflict). Neutral may be above the 2010s (Powell, Jackson Hole, 2025, via JPM NLP report). | Floor system. IORB is the main tool, ON RRP the floor, SRF a soft ceiling for EFFR, not for repo (Perli speech, 12 Nov 2024). In-band technical adjustments: EFFR within 5bp of the top prompted an IORB cut in spring 2018; RRP +5bp in June 2021 (Barclays, US short rate primer, Jan 2025). | Fed put: median cuts begin once the S&P 500 is about 25% off its 1y high, about 20% if inflation is low. Hikes persist longer when inflation is high (1973, 2022) (Willer, Ch.8). Dots since Jan 2012 replace calendar guidance (Aikin 2012). With guidance removed, count voters, not dots (JWS, Central Casting #6.1, 21 Jun 2026). | Taylor grid: core PCE 2.25-3.40 by unemployment 4.0-4.5 gives a terminal range of about 4.4-4.9 at core PCE 3.0 (BofA, Start of rates bite, 2 Oct 2026). Robust cores lagged headline by 6-8 months in 2022-26 (JPM, Lags in robust PCE cores, 13 Aug 2026). Reserve scarcity gauge: reserves over bank assets, abundant above 13%, ample 11-13%, scarce below 11% (Conks, Plumbing Notes, 23 Jul 2025; source-specific cut-offs, not a standard). |
| ECB (EUR) | Sole inflation mandate (JWS, #3, 8 Mar 2026). Official neutral deposit rate range 1.75-2.25% (R* -0.25/+0.25, JWS, Global Rates Outlook #6, 7 Jun 2026). | Floor system moving to demand-driven. Deposit rate is the key tool; QE follows capital keys with a one-third issue limit from 2015, relaxed under PEPP (Tuckman and Serrat, 2022). | Escalation ladder: (1) verbal guidance then the depo path for tight conditions, (2) balance sheet only for disorderly moves in speed or size, (3) fine-tuning QT is a high bar, (4) new LTROs or a structural portfolio unlikely, (5) TPI for disorderly unwarranted spread moves, (6) possible long-end tool (BofA, Fog of war, 2 Oct 2026; Citi, What to do about OATs, 1 Oct 2026). Adjustment hikes from neutral with a sole inflation mandate (JWS, #3). Pain threshold higher than the market's. | Energy: each $10 Brent about 30bp on near-term HICP; about $110 Brent where HICP breaks 3% (JWS, #3, 8 Mar 2026). Brent above $95 gives HICP above 4% in the adverse case (JWS, Global Rates Outlook #6, 7 Jun 2026). Fragmentation: split GDP-weighted EA 10y change into OIS and country ASW parts (Citi, What to do about OATs, 1 Oct 2026). |
| BoE (GBP) | Inflation targeting. Heuristic: set rates so expected inflation two years ahead equals target; after a large shock return over more than two years (King, Mais Lecture, 17 May 2005). | Floor system moving to demand-driven (BofA, Global Policy Implementation, 9 Jul 2025). Forecast months Feb/May/Aug/Nov. | Majority on hold with risks skewed to hikes; hike premium comes out one meeting at a time (Citi, Global Macro Strategy, 31 Jul 2026; Citi, Global Asset Allocation, 21 Aug 2026). Hikes more likely in forecast months (67% of hikes since Dec 1998 in forecast meetings, swapsball 2018, read with care). MPC votes drifted hawkish 9-0 to 7-2 (Jun 2026) then 2-7 for hikes (JWS, Global Rates Update #7, 19 Jul 2026). Energy-sensitive; OFGEM caps delay pass-through. | Market CPI path read as RPI swaps minus about 0.8%, the median historical RPI-CPI wedge, which itself moves with inflation level (JWS, #5, 10 May 2026). |
| BoJ (JPY) | Price stability, with a long history of starting late. Structural lag: "always starts late in the hiking cycle" (Willer, Ch.7). | YCC and fixed-rate purchases (BofA, Japan rates basics, 24 Apr 2023). Hikes: 2006 (50bp, quickly unwound), NIRP ended Mar 2024 (Willer, Ch.7). | Intervention-driven regime: yen defence needs an earlier hike, a September hike "necessary, if not fully sufficient" (Citi, Weekly Macro Brief, 8 Aug 2026). Dissent heuristic: the last two hikes followed meetings with at least two hawkish dissents (Citi, Global Macro Strategy, 7 Aug 2026). Back-to-back hikes rare; the market has not priced more than 25bp across two consecutive meetings for more than a day (Citi, Global Asset Allocation, 21 Aug 2026). The market has historically not priced more than about 80% of a BoJ hike until about a week before the meeting, when the hike is confirmed in the press (Citi, Global Macro Strategy, 13 Aug 2026). | Real-rate floor: the BoJ moves quickly at least until real rates are no longer negative (Citi, Japan Economics, 7 Aug 2026). USDJPY above 159 makes skipping a hike harder (Citi, Japan Rates Weekly, 14 Aug 2026). Hike-path feasibility: a hike every quarter is hard to price (Citi, Japan Rates Weekly, 14 Aug 2026). Cycle rules: front-end payers less than 1y before the first hike, held to about the last hike; Fed cuts tend to cut BoJ cycles short (Willer, Ch.7). |
| BoC (CAD) | Inflation targeting. Operating band described as a "flooridor" (BofA, Global Policy Implementation, 9 Jul 2025). Forecast months Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct (swapsball 2018). | Overnight repo is the main tool against upward CORRA pressure, usually triggered when CORRA settles 5bp above target. Term repo complements. Reserves target CAD 50-70bn (Goldman Sachs, Global Rates Trader, 2 Oct 2026). | Headline inflation at the top of range while core trim, median and ex food-energy-taxes measures sit at or below 2% means "the economy does not need higher rates" (Citi, Canada Economics Weekly, 21 Aug 2026). Tariffs are a dovish risk (Citi, Canada Economics Weekly, 13 Aug 2026). | Pricing gauge: 6m forward CORRA minus the effective rate, in bp (Citi, Canada Economics Weekly, 13 Aug 2026). |
| RBA (AUD) | Inflation targeting. Hikes more likely in SoMP months (Feb/May/Aug/Nov), about 3:1 odds per meeting relative to other months (swapsball 2018). | Moving from floor to corridor, announced Apr 2025 (BofA, Global Policy Implementation, 9 Jul 2025). | "Catch-22": a lower forecast inflation path that justifies a hold also lowers the bar for a hike (Citi, STIRT Weekly, Aug 2026). The RBA revealed a preference not to delay after its hike (Goldman Sachs, Global Rates Trader, 2 Oct 2026). | Trimmed-mean Dec-2026 inflation 3.3% in the SoMP implies +0.8% q/q in H2 (Citi, STIRT Weekly, 14 Aug 2026). |
| RBNZ (NZD) | Thin. | Thin. | Thin. Only a dated reading: Sep 2026 hike +23.5bp priced, Citi agrees (Citi, STIRT Weekly, 7 Aug 2026). | OCR end-2026 about 3.00%; 2y inflation expectations 2.34% Q3 vs 2.53% Q2 (Citi, STIRT Weekly, 14 Aug 2026). |
| SNB (CHF) | Independent of the finance ministry. Inflation mandate with an FX-intervention tool. | SARON held at the policy rate by SNB bills. Sight deposits are the intervention proxy (BofA, FX Primer, 8 Jul 2024). | Intervenes mostly in EUR/CHF. A 1.20 EUR/CHF floor from 2012 (balance sheet peaked near 150% of GDP); later CHF buying to ring-fence imported inflation (BofA, FX Primer, 8 Jul 2024). Energy weight in CPI about 5%, so low front-end beta to oil (JWS, #3, 8 Mar 2026). | Pay CHF 1y1y vs EUR 1y1y at 3.02 moved to 2.98 (Goldman Sachs, Global Rates Trader, 2 Oct 2026). |
| Riksbank (SEK) | Inflation targeting. Underlying inflation: CPIF ex energy ex tax (Citi, Nordic Economics Flash, 20 Aug 2026). | Thin. | An average-rate path that rises less than one 25bp step implies a hike probability below 100%; June MPR path averages 1.76%, 1.82%, 1.89% implied under 50% for a hike Sep to Dec (Citi, Nordic Economics Flash, 20 Aug 2026). Dovish reaction risk: hard to validate hawkish pricing (Citi, STIRT Weekly, 21 Aug 2026). | Held at 1.75%. Sep SWESTR repriced from 50% to below 35% hike probability (Citi, STIRT Weekly, 21 Aug 2026). |
| Norges Bank (NOK) | Inflation targeting. Thin on framework. | Thin. | Sep 2026 about 50% hike priced; receive front meetings vs pay further out (Citi, STIRT Weekly, 7 Aug 2026; Citi, STIRT Weekly, 14 Aug 2026). Norges more hawkish than Riksbank (Citi, Global FX Strategy: Long NOKSEK, 21 Aug 2026). | Pay 12x15 NOK FRA vs receive 12x15 SEK FRA moved 164.5 to 249.6 (Citi, Global Macro Strategy, 7 Aug 2026). |

## FX intervention (JPY, CHF, USD)

- **Who decides.** Japan: the MoF funds yen-selling with FB issuance (BofA, FX Primer, 8 Jul 2024). US: the Treasury
  decides and the NY Fed executes through the ESF plus a matching SOMA amount. The Fed usually matches roughly 50/50
  (BofA, FX Primer, 8 Jul 2024). SNB: independent of the finance ministry.
- **Triggers used in the sources.**
  - REER band: plot JPY REER against its 5-year average with plus or minus 1 and 2 sigma bands (data since 1970).
    Concerted G7 interventions occurred when REER moved at least 2 sigma from its 5-year average and tended to turn
    the long-term trend. Episodes listed: Nov 78, Plaza Sep 85, Louvre Feb 87, Jan 88, May 94, Apr 95, Apr 98,
    Sep 2000, Mar 2011, 2022 (Citi, Global FX: Twelve questions, 29 Jan 2026). A second Citi note lists a different
    set of episodes (Citi, JPY defense policy, 3/4 Aug 2026), so treat episode lists as approximate.
  - Level: intervention likely if USDJPY threatens 160. Above 162, Citi puts the probability above 50%. EURJPY warning
    zone 185-186 (Citi, Japan FX, 13/14 Aug 2026).
  - IMF free-float rule: no more than 3 rounds in 6 months, each of no more than 3 trading days. Three rounds of more
    than 3 days in 6 months would downgrade Japan to "floating" (Citi, Japan FX, 4 Aug 2026).
- **Capacity.** Original Japanese estimate of about 30trn yen. Used so far: about 11.7trn (Apr/May) + 13.8trn (Jul) =
  25.5trn, leaving about 4.5trn. A 36trn practical limit (including securities maturing within a year plus interest)
  allows about 10.5trn more. FIMA repo extends capacity beyond the stated figure. The constraint is "more about will
  than balance sheet" (Citi, Global FX Strategy: What next for JPY, 3 Aug 2026). ESF is about $217bn, mostly SDRs (Citi,
  JPY defense policy, 3/4 Aug 2026).
- **Mechanics.** US-side selling of EURJPY rather than USDJPY avoids UST selling and term-premium pressure (Citi, JPY
  defense policy, 3/4 Aug 2026). Funding through FIMA repo realises no FX gains. Selling past USD reserves realises
  gains that can fund the General Account (Citi, Bessent's plans, 13/14 Aug 2026).
- **Effects.** Intervention buys time but does not fix fundamentals (BofA, FX Primer, 8 Jul 2024). Interventions "are
  only successful if backed by a macro tailwind" (rates differential and terms of trade) (Citi, Global Macro Strategy,
  7 Aug 2026). A sharp move of about 5 yen per round (Citi, Japan FX, 31 Jul 2026). Post-intervention dollar-funding softness fades within 1-2
  weeks (Citi, STIRT Weekly, 7 Aug 2026).
- **Reaction-function shift.** Intervention can pull hikes forward ("move ahead of schedule or risk being blamed",
  FT, 21 Aug 2026). Citi moved its hike forecast to Sep and its terminal to 2.0% (Citi, Japan Economics, 7 Aug 2026).
  If policy becomes an FX tool, JPY pricing starts to behave like Fed or ECB pricing (consecutive hikes priced),
  which the source reads as a policy-error risk (Citi, Japan Rates Weekly, 2 Oct 2026).
- **Dead ends.** Japan may abandon yen defence if equities fall sharply (Citi, Twelve questions, 29 Jan 2026). The
  market assumes UST-funded intervention, but Japan used bills and cash, so further rounds may need coupon sales
  (Citi, What next for JPY, 3 Aug 2026).
